draft.title: Fight, flight or freeze
card: Fight, flight or freeze is an acute stress response. Acute means it is sudden and short, in reaction to a threat that is happening now.
The sympathetic nervous system, part of the autonomic nervous system, switches on. It prepares the body for action, for example with a faster heart rate and faster breathing.
Fight
face the threat and confront it.
Flight
run from the threat to get away. Freeze means staying very still, which can help avoid being noticed.
draft.remember: A sudden threat switches on the sympathetic system, and the body readies to fight, flee or freeze.

a.q: Which event is an example of the acute stress response?
opts: A student's heart pounds as a car swerves towards her
A student feels low after weeks of study pressure
A student sleeps deeply after a long day at school
A student slowly gets used to a noisy new classroom
a.why: A car swerving is a sudden, present threat, so the sympathetic system prepares the body to act. Weeks of study pressure is tempting, but it is a long stressor, not a sudden one.
a.clue: Look for a sudden threat happening right now.

b.q: Leo is walking in bushland and sees a snake on the track. He stops and stays completely still, hoping it does not notice him. What best describes his response?
opts: Freeze, driven by the sympathetic nervous system
Freeze, which happens when the sympathetic system is off
Flight, because he stopped moving away from the snake
Fight, because he is facing the snake directly
b.why: Staying still to avoid notice is the freeze response, and the sympathetic system is still switched on, preparing the body. Flight would mean running away, which Leo did not do.
b.clue: Is Leo moving, or keeping still to avoid being noticed?

a.best: A student's heart pounds as a car swerves towards her

b.best: Freeze, driven by the sympathetic nervous system

problems.detail: The card presents freeze as a purely sympathetic response. Many VCE resources (e.g. Jacaranda, Grivas) teach that freeze involves the parasympathetic nervous system as well, sometimes dominating, which can lower heart rate and cause immobility. The card does not mention this, and some teachers or markers may expect it.

The intended answer and its why say freeze is 'driven by the sympathetic nervous system'. Under the common VCE account, freeze involves parasympathetic as well as sympathetic activity, so this answer could be contested. Consider wording it as 'Freeze, with the sympathetic system still active' and noting the parasympathetic role.

proposal.title: Fight, flight or freeze
card: Fight, flight or freeze is an acute stress response: a sudden, short reaction to a threat happening now. The sympathetic nervous system, part of the autonomic nervous system, prepares the body to act, for example with a faster heart rate and breathing.
Fight
face the threat and confront it directly.
Flight
run or move away from the threat to escape it.
Freeze
stay very still, which can help avoid being noticed. The sympathetic system stays active, and the parasympathetic system also becomes active, which can slow the heart rate and keep the body still.
proposal.remember: A sudden threat triggers sympathetic arousal. Freeze also brings in the parasympathetic system.
